summary: Tested session bugfixes on top of iteration 5 (drift skip ONLY for admin token, PATCH clears grid_slot, Field constraint on time_sync_max_drift_seconds, alerts toggle, server-time, sla defaults). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5_session_bugfixes.py with 11 backend tests: 8 PASSED (drift skip behavior, PATCH grid_slot clearing, SLA defaults for prioridade/preventiva/venda, /api/server-time public, valid drift accepted). 3 FAILED — PUT /api/settings with invalid time_sync_max_drift_seconds (0, -10, 100000) returns 500 instead of 422 because Pydantic ValidationError raised inside the handler bubbles up unhandled. critical.issue: time_sync_max_drift_seconds=0/-10/100000 returns 500 (unhandled pydantic ValidationError) instead of 422. Field(ge=1, le=86400) is correctly defined but the handler instantiates Settings(**partial) outside FastAPI's body validation, so Pydantic ValidationError propagates as 500.

Backend bug at PUT /api/settings (500 → should be 422) is the only critical regression from this session's changes.
rca of the issue: PUT /api/settings 500: handler reads existing settings dict, merges request body, then calls Settings(**merged). Pydantic raises ValidationError (correctly enforcing Field ge=1 le=86400) but this is NOT caught — FastAPI's ValidationError translation only fires for declared request models, not for in-handler model instantiation. Mitigation: declare PUT body as `payload: SettingsUpdate` Pydantic model (with same Field constraints) so FastAPI returns 422 automatically OR wrap in try/except ValidationError as e: raise HTTPException(422, e.errors()). Reproduction: PUT /api/settings {time_sync_max_drift_seconds: 0} with admin Bearer → 500.
